chunks: He said: I was informed by al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mughairah, who reported from Abu Muhammad Haydar ibn Muhammad al-Samarqandi, who reported from Abu Amru Muhammad ibn Amru al-Kashshi, who reported from Hamdawayh ibn Nusayr, who reported from Ya'qoob ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn al-Mughairah, who said:
Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and I were in the presence of Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him. Yahya said to him: "May I be your ransom, they claim that you know the unseen."

He replied: "Glory be to God! Place your hand upon my head." By God, not a single hair on it or on my body remained except that it stood on end. Then he said: "No, by God, it is nothing but an inheritance from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family."

key_terms.الْغَيْبَ،: the unseen (al-ghayb) — knowledge of hidden matters known only to God
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to God — an exclamation of God's transcendence
key_terms.وِرَاثَةٌ: inheritance — the transmission of prophetic knowledge to the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about knowledge of the unseen (ilm al-ghayb)?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Ibn al-Mughairah recounts being present with Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan before Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the seventh Imam. When Yahya mentions that people claim the Imam has knowledge of the unseen (ilm al-ghayb), the Imam emphatically denies possessing independent knowledge of the unseen and clarifies that whatever knowledge he possesses is inherited from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW).

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: I have been informed by al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mughairah, who reported from Abu Muhammad Haider ibn Muhammad al-Samarqandi, who reported from Abu Amru Muhammad ibn Amru al-Kashi, who reported from Hamdawayh ibn Naseer, who reported from Ya’qoob ibn Yazeed, who reported from Ibn Abi Umayr, who reported from Ibn al-Mughairah who said:
Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and I were with Abul Hasan, peace be upon him, and Yahya asked him: "May I be your ransom, they think that you have the knowledge of the unseen (Ilmul Ghaib)."

He said: "Glory be to Allah! Place your hand over my head." When I did that, every hair in my head and on my body stood on its end. Then he said: "No, By Allah, it is nothing but what we have inherited from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny)."
